title: Initial outlet mixed-reach sequence
scope: Qualitative physical sequence of Project Hearthway's initial basin outlet from its bedrock-controlled throat into a connected downstream mixed reach. Exact geometry, feature count and ordering after the throat, materials, hydrology, seasonal usability, route capacity, organism compatibility, passability, human use, and System or Mana effects remain open.
approval_evidence: After A, B, and C outlet-structure options were presented, the Author replied 'C' on 2026-08-14, selecting 'C — Mixed outlet sequence'.
question: What dominant qualitative physical sequence should extend the narrow, naturally defensible outlet gap established by WLD-GEOGRAPHY-001 without pre-empting hydrology, organism fit, or passage success?
selection: Use C — Mixed outlet sequence. A narrow bedrock-controlled throat opens downstream into one connected mixed reach containing irregular boulder steps, lateral or side shelves, and local holding pockets. The reach is heterogeneous rather than one uniform channel or regular feature chain. Boulder steps and side shelves are candidate, state-dependent bed-or-margin contact surfaces against which WLD-ECOLOGY-010 passage can be tested. Holding pockets are local channel recesses or pools that may be less exposed to the main flow under some conditions and can be tested as potentially lower-velocity locations. Coherent migration corridor means only one connected physical system and candidate route architecture; it does not establish a continuous support or rest chain, guaranteed low velocity, safety, recovery, passability, seasonal usability, route capacity, or organism success.
alternatives: A — Bedrock step-pool chain: low stone sills alternating with shallow basins and deeper pools; not selected.
B — Alternating margin shelves: a central channel bordered by staggered ledges, backwaters, and eddies; not selected.
C — Mixed outlet sequence: a narrow bedrock throat opening into a connected mixed reach containing irregular boulder steps, side shelves, and holding pockets; selected.
rationale: The selected option is the smallest forward extension that turns the wholly open outlet profile into a connected qualitative feature set. Its heterogeneity permits later state-dependent hydrology and organism-fit testing while preserving all quantitative, seasonal, ecological, and outcome uncertainty.
evidence: Author selection on 2026-08-14: after A, B, and C outlet-structure options were presented, the Author replied 'C', selecting 'C — Mixed outlet sequence'.
consequences: The narrow bedrock-controlled throat precedes a downstream mixed reach containing irregular boulder steps, lateral or side shelves, and local holding pockets; no exact count, spacing, or order among the downstream features is selected.
The reach is one connected physical system, but no continuous support, rest, or movement chain is established.
Boulder steps and side shelves are only candidate contacts whose wetting, exposure, stability, accessibility, and load-bearing suitability remain state dependent and untested.

Holding pockets are local channel recesses or pools that may be less exposed to the main flow under some conditions; they are not guaranteed low-velocity water, refuges, safe zones, checkpoints, healing sites, recovery sites, or refill points.
Exact flow, depth, discharge, gradient, turbulence, water level, flood, ice, debris, tidal, salinity, erosion, and deposition behaviour remains open.

WLD-ECOLOGY-010 passage can be tested against the accepted feature set, but actual contact fit, support continuity, resting opportunity, seasonal viability, passability, and organism success remain unresolved.

WLD-ECOLOGY-006 continues to govern the qualitative migration and freshet relationship, WLD-ECOLOGY-009 continues to govern the body plan and route-feasibility concern, and WLD-ECOLOGY-010 continues to govern organism-side passage choreography.
Material, water, usable energy, route space, organism condition, injury, mortality, recruitment, and recovery remain finite and causal.
Visible channel form and local conditions do not reveal hidden hydraulics, physiology, annual route capacity, seasonal usability, passability, or species-wide success.
No exact geology, inhabitant, habitat occupancy, human structure or use, cultural practice, Mana property, System interaction, spawn, reset, refill, reward, or guaranteed recovery is created.
residual_unknowns: Exact map, place names, dimensions, elevations, gradients, cross-sections, distances, and travel times remain open.
Exact lithology, boulder source, sediments, landform origin, formation chronology, erosion, deposition, movement, and feature stability remain open.
Number, order after the throat, spacing, continuity, geometry, dimensions, and seasonal exposure of all downstream features remain open.
Discharge, velocity, depth, turbulence, eddies, water levels, floods, ice, debris, water chemistry, tidal reach, salinity transition, and storm surge remain open.
Which surfaces are accessible or load-bearing and which pockets are less exposed to main flow under particular conditions remain open.
Continuous support or rest availability, seasonal usability, route capacity, passage timing, organism fit, fatigue, injury, recovery, mortality, and success remain open.
Habitat occupancy, species use, food webs, predation, disease, competition, carrying capacity, and ecological recovery remain open.
Human travel, crossing, fishing, settlement, defence, ownership, naming, knowledge, law, trade, ritual, folklore, and conflict remain open.
Mana properties, System interactions, ancient-doorway relationships, and offworld influence remain open.
reopening_conditions: Later geomorphology or hydrology cannot support any coherent version of the selected throat-to-mixed-reach structure.
Later migration modelling cannot test a viable candidate route architecture without contradicting WLD-ECOLOGY-006, WLD-ECOLOGY-009, or WLD-ECOLOGY-010.
A later accepted map, ecology, settlement, or story record creates a concrete contradiction.
The Author explicitly requests a different outlet structure.
